newsitem.title: USA: Universal unveils new Florida theme park.
newsitem.headline: Universal unveils new Florida theme park.

text.p: Universal Studios unveiled plans Tuesday for yet another theme park in Florida's crowded fantasy corridor, this one dividing its devotion between comic strip characters and the born-again dinosaurs of Jurassic Park.

The company made the announcement that it will build Universal's Islands of Adventure without the expected presence of director Steve Spielberg, who begged off with a cold, but with plenty of fireworks and cartoon creators nonetheless.
Islands of Adventure will open alongside Universal Studios Florida and together they will be known as Universal City Florida, company officials said.

Universal's move is at least partially a response to Disney's Animal Kingdom, a new theme park set to open in Walt Disney World next year, but also to the growth in international tourist traffic headed to Orlando.

"Orlando is already the world's No. 1 tourist destination," Universal City Florida President Tom Williams said. "We're putting more money here than in (Universal Studios) Hollywood because you have two things in Orlando you don't find anywhere else -- a great airport and good weather year round."
Company officials said the first part of the project, a 12-acre restaurant and nightclub complex, would open next year and the remainder in 1999. They did not reveal the cost of the project.

To open a preview exhibition of the five theme islands the park will feature, Spider-Man made a grand entrance over Universal's studio back lot. Meanwhile, Captain America, The Hulk, Bullwinkle, Popeye and Betty Boop, among others, made a more prosaic entrance from the rear of a tractor-trailer rig.

Stan Lee, publisher of Marvel Comics and creator of many characters to be featured on Marvel Super Hero Island, said he was not worried that his super-heroes may not be the drawing card that Spielberg's dinosaurs or Disney's cartoon icons have proven to be.

"These comic characters are a part of every young person's experience," Lee said. "I'm always meeting writers, doctors and teachers who start telling me how much they enjoyed them as kids, then say something like, 'Why did they do that in X-Men last month?' Then I realise they're still reading them."

Alongside Lee's costumed do-gooders and Spielberg's Jurassic carnivores, will be islands devoted to the characters of Dr. Seuss, to comic strip and cartoon favourites and to adventure and fantasy from the age of fable. Universal Studios is a subsidiary of Seagram Company Ltd.
